thread:
Elliot Price: Heads up docs coordination thread for Hardware tuning profiles pack (runtime-1.22). Need to lock: (1) where Confluence pages live, (2) reviewers/owners, (3) which tables are required so we don’t ship another wall of text.

Kira Thompson: +1. Can we keep everything under the existing Eng Serving Runtime space? Folks keep creating one-offs.

Elliot Price: Proposal for Confluence hierarchy (matches the outline Mateo shared):
- Eng > Serving Runtime > Kernel and Scheduling
  - Hardware tuning profiles pack overview
  - Profile schema + selection rules
  - Expected behavior: H100
  - Expected behavior: L40S
  - Expected behavior: B200 (preview)
- Eng > Serving Runtime > Benchmarking and perf suite
  - Benchmark matrix + acceptance thresholds
- Eng > Serving Runtime > Profiling playbook
  - How to validate a new hardware profile
- Architecture and standards > Decision records
  - ADR-041 hardware tuning profiles pack
- Eng > SRE > SLO and error budgets
  - Profile rollout SLO guardrails
- Eng > Platform > Dashboards and alerts
  - Runtime profile observability dashboard spec

Mateo Alvarez: That structure looks right. Please don’t put engineering runbooks in Product space :)

Connor O'Brien: Works for release. Only callout: release notes page should live under Eng > Serving Runtime > Release notes (runtime-1.22) so we can link it in the train email.

Elliot Price: Yep. I’ll add: Eng > Serving Runtime > Release notes > runtime-1.22 profile pack launch.

Allison Grant: For the observability spec page, can we also cross-link from the overview doc? People will ask “what do I look at” during canary.

Elliot Price: Definitely. Now review assignments (suggested). Please react :thumbsup: or propose changes:
- Overview doc: owner @Mateo Alvarez, reviewers @Neha Kapoor @Lauren Bishop @Rafael Mendes
- Schema + selection rules: owner @Omar El-Sayed, reviewers @Hiro Tanaka @Sofia Ivanova @Connor O'Brien
- Expected behavior H100: owner @Hiro Tanaka, reviewers @Allison Grant @Rafael Mendes
- Expected behavior L40S: owner @Sofia Ivanova, reviewers @Neha Kapoor @Omar El-Sayed
- Expected behavior B200 preview: owner @Neha Kapoor, reviewers @Hiro Tanaka @Allison Grant
- Benchmark matrix + acceptance: owner (Applied ML) but for now I’ll put @Omar El-Sayed as editor until Jonas/Claire confirm. Reviewers @Sofia Ivanova @Connor O'Brien
- Validation playbook: owner @Rafael Mendes, reviewers @Kira Thompson @Allison Grant
- Rollout SLO guardrails: owner @Rafael Mendes, reviewers @Neha Kapoor @Mateo Alvarez
- Dashboard spec: owner @Allison Grant, reviewers @Omar El-Sayed @Rafael Mendes

Hiro Tanaka: :thumbsup: on H100 expected behavior ownership.

Sofia Ivanova: :thumbsup: for L40S. I might need a quick sanity review from Lena/Marcus on concurrency caps once the last rerun lands, but fine.

Neha Kapoor: :thumbsup: B200 preview. I’ll need the driver/CUDA baseline paragraph to be explicit (what we support vs “works on my node”).

Lauren Bishop: :thumbsup: overview reviewer. For Dedicated, I want a small “what changes for customers / how to pin” callout in overview + link to customer messaging draft.

Elliot Price: Great. Last item: required tables. I’d like these included everywhere relevant so SRE/support has copy/paste reference.

Kira Thompson: Please make tables consistent (same column names). Otherwise people can’t compare SKUs.

Elliot Price: Proposed REQUIRED tables (please comment if you think any are overkill):
1) Profile selection summary (on overview + schema pages)
   - Columns: deployment_mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), selection_source (fleet default / pinned / override), precedence, auditability (Y/N), rollback mechanism
2) Compatibility matrix (schema page + B200 preview)
   - Columns: gpu_sku, form_factor (SXM/PCIe if relevant), driver_min, cuda_min, mig_supported (Y/N), notes
3) Default knob summary per SKU (each expected behavior page)
   - Columns: knob, default_value, rationale, risk_if_overridden, observability_signal
   - Keep knob names exactly as in config (snake_case)
4) Workload buckets + targets (each expected behavior page)
   - Columns: bucket_name, prompt_tokens_range, decode_tokens_range, concurrency_range, expected_behavior (p95/p99 notes), failure_modes
5) Known failure modes + mitigations (each expected behavior page + validation playbook)
   - Columns: symptom, likely_cause, signal_to_check (metric/log), immediate_mitigation, longer_term_fix, owner_team
6) Bench acceptance thresholds (benchmark matrix page)
   - Columns: sku, model_family, bucket_name, metric, baseline, allowed_delta, hard_fail (Y/N)
7) Rollout gates (SRE guardrails page)
   - Columns: metric, window, threshold, action (block/rollback/page), notes

Allison Grant: For (3) “observability_signal” column, can we constrain to metric names we actually export? I can provide canonical metric names + tags so docs doesn’t drift.

Elliot Price: Yes, please. If you can drop the canonical names here I’ll paste them into the template.

Allison Grant: Canonical metrics/tags for the docs tables:
- `runtime_request_latency_ms` (tags: `profile_id`, `sku`, `model`, `route`, `stage=prefill|decode|total`)
- `scheduler_queue_ms` (tags: `profile_id`, `sku`, `bucket`)
- `kernel_choice` counter (tags: `sku`, `kernel_family`, `variant`, `reason`)
- `kernel_fallback_total` counter (tags: `sku`, `reason`)
- `kv_cache_hit_rate` gauge (tags: `sku`, `profile_id`)
- `kv_compaction_ms` histogram (tags: `sku`, `profile_id`)
- `gpu_oom_total` counter (tags: `sku`, `profile_id`, `phase=prefill|decode`)
- `allocator_fragmentation_estimate` gauge (tags: `sku`, `profile_id`)

Rafael Mendes: For rollout gates table (7), can we explicitly include “canary cohort” and “kill-switch” link? On-call will ask where the button is.

Connor O'Brien: +1. Also on release notes, please include a “What changed vs 1.21” table:
- Columns: area (scheduler/kernel/memory/obs), change, expected impact, rollback steps, tracking ticket.

Mateo Alvarez: Agree on all tables. If anything, it’s the only way we keep this sane.

Omar El-Sayed: On schema + selection rules, I’ll include: example YAML snippet + a “precedence diagram” section, but tables are fine. Also will add an explicit note: Dedicated customer pins require audit log entry.

Elliot Price: Action items:
- I’ll create the Confluence pages under the paths above today and paste links in ENG-4921.
- Owners: please fill in your pages by EOD Thu so we can do doc review Fri before go/no-go.
- @Kira Thompson I’ll share a docs template with the table headers so everyone copies the same structure.

Kira Thompson: :thumbsup: send template. Also please add a top-of-page “last validated with profile_version X.Y.Z” line so Support can tell if they’re reading stale guidance.

Elliot Price: Good call. Adding “Validated with profile_version” + “Last updated” at the top of each expected behavior page.

DocsBot: Reminder set by Elliot Price: "Profile pack doc owners fill pages" in 2 days.
